messages:
Anjali: Quick proposal — add a "safety_score" to the config preview API and a server-side gate for canary rollouts. If safety_score < 0.8, block automatic canary promotion and mark as REVIEW.
Tom: How would we compute safety_score?
Anjali: Combine a small set of signals: p95 latency delta, 5xx error rate delta, request success ratio, and eval set regression (if available). Weighted average with tunable thresholds per-tenant.
Kevin: Do we compute that in the console (frontend) or runtime (server)? Need it server-side so CLI / API users get consistent behavior.
Maya: Agree server-side. Also we should sample windows: compare the candidate rollout traffic to a baseline window (last 30m) to avoid noise.
Anjali: Right — propose preview endpoint returns: { safety_score: 0.73, reasons: ["p95 +12%","5xx +0.8%"] } and a flag "blocked": true/false.
Tom: API shape nit: prefer POST /api/config/preview with body {config, sample_spec, safety_mode:"block|warn"} so we can run heavier telemetry queries without exposing them in GET.
Kevin: Works for me. Also add a short "rollback_hint" string in the response, e.g. "suggested: reduce batch_size to 8 or use quantized-variant". Helps ops.
Maya: Telemetry caveat — baseline drift for low-volume tenants will be noisy. We should surface a confidence score and require a min-sample cutoff before we evaluate safety (or default to warn).
Anjali: Agreed. Proposal: safety_score = null + reason "insufficient_data" when samples < min. And console shows a big yellow banner.
Kevin: Implementation plan: 1) preview API + safety calc in control plane service, 2) expose reasons and rollback_hint, 3) console: block/override UX + link to eval traces.
Tom: How do we want rollouts to interact with existing dry-run mode? I think dry-run should *always* run safety checks but not block — only canary promotion uses the mode param.
Maya: Also add telemetry hooks: emit a preview.safety_check event with tags for tenant_id, config_id, sample_count, safety_score, reasons. That makes auditing + metric dashboards easy.
sre-bot: Note: if a rollout is blocked we should automatically create a P0-lite page for the owning team or at least open a ticket to ops with the preview payload.
Anjali: Example curl (for review):
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/config/preview -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"config": {"route_policy": "priority"}, "safety_mode": "block", "sample_spec": {"window_mins":30}}'
```
Tom: Looks good. Can we add an opt-in flag for "run_eval": true to run the small regression eval harness during preview?
Kevin: Yes but make it async with a separate eval_result link in the response (don't hold the preview call).
Maya: One last ask — add an escape hatch for platform-admins to force-promo if blocked (audit + 2-person approval).
Anjali: Will draft a short RFC with API contract, telemetry events, and console mockups. Tagging @Kevin and @Maya for implementation owners.
Kevin: ack.
Maya: ack.
sre-bot: Action created: preview-safety-gate RFC assigned to Anjali, due EOD Fri.
